subject.title: perf: avoid event-loop stall during embedded_run bootstrap-context

question: Should core permanently own a custom asynchronous glob walker and yield between `agent:bootstrap` handlers to protect gateway responsiveness, rather than retain Node’s native traversal and uninterrupted hook scheduling?
rationale: The patch is technically coherent and proof-positive, but this choice establishes long-lived compatibility and plugin-observability behavior that cannot be resolved mechanically from tests alone.

options.title: Adopt the owned runtime contract
options.body: Accept the cooperative walker and hook scheduling after a core owner confirms that the tested parity boundary is the supported contract.

options.title: Narrow the approach
options.body: Keep the performance objective but ask for an owner-approved alternative that avoids maintaining custom glob semantics or changing hook interleaving.

options.title: Pause the PR
options.body: Defer this optimization if core does not want to own the compatibility and scheduling surface it introduces.

recommendation.title: Adopt the owned runtime contract
recommendation.body: Accept the cooperative walker and hook scheduling after a core owner confirms that the tested parity boundary is the supported contract.

likelyOwner.reason: The timeline directly routes this core-runtime review to steipete; no stronger file-history owner could be established from the supplied read-only context.
